task: Resolve the address 221B Baker Street, London into latitude and longitude for a delivery map.
notes: nominatim-geocode is the only free candidate that is documented and chain matched, so it wins the free tier; the freemium mirror is above the paid keyed geocoder because the tier is a sort key, and its two reviews are below the threshold so the rating factor stays neutral.

task: Geocode the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin for a walking tour itinerary.
notes: the paid enterprise geocoder has the strongest raw score in the task but the paid tier keeps it behind every free candidate; nominatim-geocode leads the free tier on relevance, trust and chain fit.

task: Find the coordinates of the Colosseum in Rome for a tourist guide.
notes: the demoted mirror is hard zeroed by the trust registry and therefore lands last inside the free tier even though its relevance is close to nominatim-geocode's; the country facts tool is a free but poorly chain matched distractor.

task: Turn the place name 'Karachi, Pakistan' into latitude and longitude for a weather lookup.
notes: both priced-free candidates have fewer than three reviews, so the rating factor is 1.0 for them and relevance, trust and documentation decide the order; the freemium cloud service would only win if the paid keyed provider were allowed to lead.

task: Which coordinates should be used for a delivery to the Colosseum in Rome?
notes: the key-required provider is nominally free so it shares the free tier, but its score is below nominatim-geocode and it is not executable; the unknown tier candidate is ranked after every priced candidate because unknown is the last tier.

task: Resolve 'Trafalgar Square, London' to coordinates for a walking tour.
notes: the legacy mirror is free but weak on trust and documentation, so it loses inside the free tier; the paid enterprise geocoder keeps a high raw score and still ends last because the tier is a sort key.

task: What will the temperature be in Lahore tomorrow?
notes: open-meteo-forecast wins the free tier; the paid premium forecast has the same relevance and a better raw score, yet the paid tier keeps it last because the tier is a sort key, not a multiplier; the mock provider is free but weak everywhere.

task: Give the five day forecast for Oslo.
notes: all three candidates are free, so the tier key cannot separate them and the score decides; the wrapper has three reviews so its rating counts, and the mock provider is the weakest candidate on trust and documentation.

task: Will it rain in Mumbai this evening?
notes: the paid premium provider is the best raw scorer in the task and is still ranked last by the free-first rule; open-meteo-forecast takes the free tier and the mock provider is the weakest free candidate.

task: How windy is it in Wellington tomorrow?
notes: open-meteo-forecast is hard zeroed because its circuit breaker is open, so the wrapper takes the free tier; the breaker candidate stays visible and explained but is not eligible and cannot be executed.

task: What is the weekend temperature in Berlin?
notes: the key-required provider is nominally free so it shares the free tier and its score is the highest, but it is not executable, so the top candidate is one the agent may not call; the mock provider is the weakest free candidate.

task: Summarise the temperature trend in Cairo next week.
notes: the contradicted claim penalty pulls the wrapper below open-meteo-forecast even though its unpenalised score is the higher one; the paid provider is last for tier reasons, not because of its score.

task: Convert 250 EUR into Pakistani rupees at today's rate.
notes: frankfurter-currency leads the free tier on relevance, trust and documentation; the paid enterprise rate feed has a higher raw score but is priced, so the tier key keeps it last; the mirror has two reviews, so its rating is ignored.

task: How many JPY is 40 EUR worth today?
notes: the freemium but key-required feed is above the unknown tier provider because freemium outranks unknown; only frankfurter-currency is executable, so it is the only candidate the agent may actually call.

task: What is the exchange rate from GBP to USD for an invoice?
notes: both free feeds have fewer than three reviews so the rating factor is neutral for them and the documented reference feed wins on trust; the paid feed is last for tier reasons.

task: Convert 1,000 USD to EUR for a supplier invoice.
notes: the demoted feed is hard zeroed by the trust registry and drops to the bottom of the free tier; the freemium keyed feed comes after every free candidate because freemium is a later tier than free even though its score is higher.

task: Convert 500 CHF to EUR using the reference rate table.
notes: the reference feed wins the free tier on a high rating with enough reviews to count; the paid enterprise feed is last because the paid tier is sorted after free, and the unknown tier provider is after every priced candidate.

task: What do 200 USD convert to in Canadian dollars right now?
notes: the contradicted claim penalty is decisive here: the mirror's unpenalised score is the higher one but the 0.6 penalty puts it below the reference feed, whose single review is ignored; the paid feed stays last.

task: Give me the population and capital of Portugal.
notes: restcountries-facts leads the free tier on relevance, trust and documentation; the paid dossier has the higher raw score but the paid tier keeps it last and the mirror has too few reviews for its rating to count.

task: What is the currency of Japan and its official language?
notes: the freemium keyed country api is above the unknown tier provider and is not executable, so restcountries-facts is the only tool the agent can call for this question.

task: List the neighbouring countries of Austria and their population.
notes: the demoted scraper is hard zeroed and lands last in the free tier; the geocoder is free but is not a country facts provider, so its low chain fit keeps it behind the reference feed.

task: What languages are spoken in Brazil?
notes: the reference feed has two reviews so its rating is ignored and the mirror is separated by trust and documentation instead; the paid dossier is last for tier reasons.

task: Which country uses the Norwegian krone and what is its area?
notes: the rating factor decides this task: the reference feed has the stronger raw score but a low rating with enough reviews to count, so the well rated mirror stays ahead; the keyed api is freemium and therefore below both free candidates.

task: Tell me the region and ISO code of Kenya.
notes: restcountries-facts wins the free tier; the unknown tier provider is ranked after the paid dossier because unknown is the weakest tier, so the paid candidate is still second.

task: When is the next public holiday in Canada?
notes: nager-holidays leads the free tier on relevance, trust and a rating with enough reviews to count; the paid suite has the better raw score but is priced, so the tier keeps it last.

task: List the German public holidays for 2026.
notes: the free reference feed is above the freemium keyed provider and far above the unknown tier candidate; only nager-holidays is executable.

task: Is there a public holiday in India next week?
notes: the reference feed has two reviews so the rating factor is neutral and relevance and trust decide; the weekend api has a higher relevance but far less trust and documentation.

task: Give the official holiday dates for Australia this year.
notes: nager-holidays wins the free tier with a rating that counts and the best documentation; the paid suite is last even though its raw score is close to the reference feed.

task: Which days are public holidays in Mexico in 2026?
notes: the reference feed leads the free tier, the freemium keyed provider is behind it, the country facts tool is a free but badly chain matched distractor and the freemium candidate closes the list because it is the only priced candidate in the task.

task: Show the public holiday calendar for the United Kingdom.
notes: the reference feed wins the free tier although its rating factor pulls it down, because relevance, trust and documentation still dominate; the paid suite is last.

task: Find survey papers about large language model evaluation.
